From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2024 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly readiness: initial action grid + Nova dossier draft

Nice start — added a separate "Delivery & Technical Risk" sheet in the action grid with the items I think we must call out to leadership:

- Integration complexity: Nova wants a two-way connector to their on-prem data lake (SFTP + SQL). Estimate: 4-6 weeks dev + 2-week validation window.
- Latency SLAs: they asked for sub-250ms 95p for the chat endpoint; we should note fallback model plan (quantized variant) if this can't be met in early deployment.
- Compliance asks: include the SOC2 evidence path and KMS/HSM handling — I added links to the security binder.

Also flagged two deals in the dossier where procurement is already asking for a PO: marked them "Procurement L20".

One ask: Mateo, can you confirm whether the customer will accept a pilot contract with usage caps (we proposed 2M tokens) or whether they need committed capacity day-one? That changes pricing language in the leadership slide.

Karthik
Director, Platform Delivery

Thanks — incorporated your comments and asked Ana (customer) one question about committed capacity. Summary of updates attached: consolidated action grid, dossier with per-account bullets, and a risk heatmap.

Key changes I made: 
- Reworked the ARR case: included both conservative and aggressive (best case) lanes, with clear markup of assumptions.
- Added pilot vs committed recommendation: recommend pilot + scale (two-phase) to de-risk the early implementation — this preserves runway while protecting our unit economics.
- Account notes: split "engagement health" into green/amber/red and called out procurement posture for each sub-account.

Attachments: 20240419_QBR_action_grid_v2.xlsx, Nova-Account-Dossier-Master_v2.docx, deal-risk-heatmap.png

Team — thanks for the rapid turnaround. Quick executive notes (ready to drop into the leadership deck):

1) One-liner for deck: "Nova Analytics — high-fit opportunity; phased pilot recommended to validate latency and data integration; revenue runway enclosed (conservative/aggressive)."
2) Top 3 risks: Integration complexity, procurement timeline, SLA delta for production latency.
3) Ask for leadership: directional approval to present pilot pricing (cap: 2M tokens, 3-month pilot) with a committed cadence option at 6 months.

Customer update: Ana confirmed that procurement prefers to see a committed SKU at pilot start (Net60). I flagged the revenue recognition and pricing impact in the action grid. Ana and Mark are on copy to surface any last-minute clarifications.

I think we can close language on the executive slide today if there are no objections. If everyone is good, I'll move this into the master deck and ping Sam for the slide slot.

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
